title: Optional dropout, modes and saved masks
description: Terms for training masks, their saved gradients, explicit evaluation identity and checked random-counter ownership.

terms.definition: An optional training transformation that randomly zeros individual elements of a complete projected residual branch. The course default disables it, and its correctness fixtures do not establish a model-quality improvement.
One minus the requested drop probability. A saved mask bit of one means keep and zero means drop. The one-half fixture uses a training scale of two.
The convention that rescales kept elements during training by the reciprocal of keep probability. Evaluation returns the original input handle without training rescaling or sampling.
The keep/drop choices and scale retained from one forward through a constant multiplier. Backward reuses those coefficients rather than sampling again or inferring choices from zero outputs.

The transformed attention or feed-forward contribution added to an unchanged residual input. This policy applies dropout after the complete attention output projection or SwiGLU down-projection and before the corresponding addition.

Explicit per-call choices that control sampling independently of autograd recording. Train samples at positive probability even under no-grad; Eval and zero probability return the input handle without creating a dropout operation.

The checked next-word position owned by optional dropout purpose four. Fresh active forwards commit their reserved ranges on complete success; bound site replay reuses original ranges without advancing the live counter. Equal seeds alone do not remove layout or environment constraints.
